# Sources

This appendix contains only public, reader-verifiable references. Claims should
distinguish official mechanism documentation, public package documentation,
public source observations, public test assertions, and editorial proposals.

## S7 mechanism documentation

- [S7 package site and vignettes](https://rconsortium.github.io/S7/)
- [Classes and objects](https://rconsortium.github.io/S7/articles/classes-objects.html)
- [Generics and methods](https://rconsortium.github.io/S7/articles/generics-methods.html)
- [`S7::new_property()` reference](https://rconsortium.github.io/S7/reference/new_property.html)
- [S7 repository and public tests](https://github.com/RConsortium/S7)
- [Public S4 property-type discussion](https://github.com/RConsortium/S7/issues/587)

Official documentation is the authority for supported mechanisms.
Version-sensitive runtime claims should also identify released R and S7
versions used by a reproducible probe.

## Principal public exhibits

### rtemis

- [Repository and source](https://github.com/rtemis-org/rtemis)
- [`PropertySpec` and property declarations](https://github.com/rtemis-org/rtemis/blob/main/R/010_Props.R)
- [Immutable `PropertySpec` source at revision `f60ac02`](https://github.com/rtemis-org/rtemis/blob/f60ac02b32f58373a2ba7f965b9c1c450dd2200a/R/010_Props.R)

**Public source observation.** The linked implementation supports the
chapter's claims about constraints as data, separate tuning intent, defaults,
conditional applicability, contextual data bounds, and multiple consumers.
Whether every generated projection remains aligned is an obligation proposed
by the chapter, not a fact inferred from one implementation.

### deputy

- [Repository and README](https://github.com/JamesHWade/deputy)
- [Package site](https://jameshwade.github.io/deputy/)
- [Getting started](https://jameshwade.github.io/deputy/articles/getting-started.html)
- [Permissions](https://jameshwade.github.io/deputy/articles/permissions.html)
- [Runtime integration](https://jameshwade.github.io/deputy/articles/runtime-integration.html)
- [Immutable repository snapshot at revision `2a4bda5`](https://github.com/JamesHWade/deputy/tree/2a4bda56ae6a6aa35a2f04da208850998ee3ddcb)

**Public package documentation and source observation.** These sources support
the distinction among declarative tools and policies, host-enforced
permissions, live agent execution, streaming, and completed run results.
The chapter's ownership vocabulary is an editorial interpretation of those
public mechanisms.

### sqlr

- [Repository and README](https://github.com/nbenn/sqlr)
- [Immutable README at revision `8325581`](https://github.com/nbenn/sqlr/blob/8325581ad859b408408738dcc289bcad05360d58/README.md)
- [Public generic definitions at revision `8325581`](https://github.com/nbenn/sqlr/blob/8325581ad859b408408738dcc289bcad05360d58/R/generics.R)

**Public documentation and source observation.** The README and generic
definitions support the claims about a semantic schema representation shared
by rendering, reflection, equality, and diffing; dialect objects; refusal of a
generic fallback; dependency-aware rendering; and bounded reflection. Calling
this an “earned IR” is the chapter's editorial evaluation.

## Focused contrasts

### S7schema

- [CRAN package page and manual](https://cran.r-project.org/package=S7schema)

**Official package documentation.** The package page and manual support the
claims that YAML content is validated against JSON Schema through AJV/V8 and
that S7 supplies surrounding configuration and extension machinery. The
authority comparison with stacbuildr is editorial synthesis.

### resultr

- [Repository](https://github.com/TransGirlCodes/resultr)
- [Result implementation](https://github.com/TransGirlCodes/resultr/blob/main/R/Result.R)
- [Immutable `Result` implementation at revision `0f53d4e`](https://github.com/TransGirlCodes/resultr/blob/0f53d4ee03138cc93a3feef4900746f672d12fe8/R/Result.R)

**Public source observation.** The implementation supports the claims about
`Success` and `Failure`, short-circuiting `and_then()`, and the
`wrap_in_result()` adapter between conditions and values. The recommendation
to choose one deliberate boundary is editorial.

### stacbuildr

- [Public package site](https://stevenpawley.r-universe.dev/stacbuildr)
- [Repository](https://github.com/stevenpawley/stacbuildr)
- [Immutable repository snapshot at revision `5706144`](https://github.com/stevenpawley/stacbuildr/tree/5706144faf29071e7158f4b645512d01638d76a2)

**Public package documentation and source observation.** These sources support
the claims about STAC document classes, validation against published schemas,
native geospatial boundary constructors, and tabular or spatial projections.
The claim that the native layer and external schema have different authority
is editorial synthesis.

## Additional exhibits used in prose

### quickr

- [Repository](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/quickr)
- [Published source mirror](https://rdrr.io/cran/quickr/src/R/quick.R)
- [Immutable `quick.R` source at revision `edd4037`](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/quickr/blob/edd403766e612ef4867ad817ead3dc366dc15d77/R/quick.R)
- [Immutable repository snapshot at revision `edd4037`](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/quickr/tree/edd403766e612ef4867ad817ead3dc366dc15d77)

**Public source observation.** The source supports the bounded claim that
quickr compiles R toward Fortran and passes structured, typed artifacts such
as `FortranSubroutine` through compilation. The broader lesson that a typed IR
must be earned by analysis and translation is editorial.

### typedjson

- [Repository](https://github.com/nbenn/typedjson)
- [Immutable README at revision `7160c06`](https://github.com/nbenn/typedjson/blob/7160c060e260bec3d284c39e51a9a5331779aa14/README.md)

**Public package documentation.** The README supports the claims that ordinary
values remain readable JSON, annotations are introduced for distinctions JSON
cannot preserve, and the intended law is an R-value round trip. “Minimum
metadata” is the chapter's summary of that documented design.

### s7contract

- [Repository](https://github.com/sounkou-bioinfo/s7contract)
- [CRAN package page](https://cran.r-project.org/package=s7contract)
- [Immutable README at revision `41dce50`](https://github.com/sounkou-bioinfo/s7contract/blob/41dce50d482ad4bfac382e859662abcae0ba56c4/README.md)

**Official package documentation and public source observation.** These
sources support the claims about structural interfaces, explicit traits,
runtime argument and return contracts, and generative laws with shrinking.
The limits of sampled laws are an editorial caution, not a package guarantee.

### optimizers7 and parameters7

- [optimizers7 repository](https://github.com/statmodels7/optimizers7)
- [parameters7 repository](https://github.com/statmodels7/parameters7)
- [Immutable optimizers7 README at revision `c50e414`](https://github.com/statmodels7/optimizers7/blob/c50e41416c411b530124f2329679cdc72ec85ff0/README.md)
- [Immutable parameters7 README at revision `21076ad`](https://github.com/statmodels7/parameters7/blob/21076ad92cd2442b8be767d1b0546f7f783937c5/README.md)

**Public package documentation.** The linked READMEs support the claims that
stopping rules are modeled separately and compositionally, and that
constrained parameters expose reusable maps, inverses, and derivatives. The
decision threshold for promoting policy to an object is editorial.

Ellmer appears in the deputy discussion only to identify the public chat
abstraction with which deputy composes; the linked official documentation is
the source for that identification. The remaining packages are retained as
descriptive public references used elsewhere in the book. Inclusion is not a
claim about popularity, maturity, or comparative quality.

## Evidence labels

- **Official mechanism:** documented by S7 or another authoritative public
  specification.
- **Public source observation:** visible in a linked public repository;
  behavior may change. Version-sensitive observations should use an immutable
  revision link.
- **Public test assertion:** encoded in a linked package test suite.
- **Released-version probe:** reproducible execution naming R, S7, and package
  versions.
- **Editorial proposal:** guidance offered for evaluation, not a claim that a
  package implements it.

A source comment, README statement, or single implementation can motivate a
question. It should not become a universal claim without corroborating
evidence.
